textbookText: Plasmodium is a protozoan parasite that causes dreadful disease called malaria in human beings and other animals. There are more than fifty known species of Plasmodium, causing such disease in man and other animals like lizards, birds and other mammals. So, they are commonly called malarial fever parasites. Among them, four species of Plasmodium namely Plasmodium vivax, Plasmodium malariae, Plasmodium ovale, Plasmodium falciparum are most common to human beings causing different types of malaria.

Habit and habitat: Plasmodium vivax is distributed in the temperate or warmer region of the world such as Nepal, India, and Sri Lanka, Bangladesh etc. It is an intracellular blood parasite in human, thriving in RBC and liver cells but it is extracellular in female Anopheles mosquito living in gut and salivary glands. Female Anopheles mosquito is also called vector since it is the carrier of Plasmodium parasite from malaria infected person to healthy person. Plasmodium vivax causes tertian malaria in human which is characterized by a 48-hour cycle between the first malaria fever and subsequent recurrence of chills and fever. Do you know? In the past, it was believed that the cause of malaria is bad air or foul gases of marshy areas and hence the name malaria (Gr; mala=bad; aria=air) was given. Later in 1880, Charles Laveran reported for the first time that blood of malarial patient contains Plasmodium as parasites. But it was in mystery for a long time that how these parasites were transmitted to human beings. Then, Patrick Mason in 1894 suggested that there is role of mosquitoes in the transmission of this disease from person to person.

Food vacuoles containing hemozoin are also found scattered in cytoplasm. iv. The endoplasmic reticulum is in the form of simple vesicles of variable shape and the vesicles may be rough or smooth. v. Life cycle An organism which harbors parasites is known as host. Plasmodium vivax is the digenetic parasite; completing its life cycle in two hosts: Female Anopheles mosquito and human. In this case, humans suffer from malaria but mosquitoes are not harmed. Female Anopheles mosquito is considered primary host as sexual phases of life cycle of the parasites are passed in it whereas human is referred secondary host in which Plasmodium completes its asexual cycle. The female Anopheles mosquito is also called a vector as it transmits malarial parasites from one host to another. 1. Asexual life cycle of Plasmodium vivax in human a. Infection or inoculation of sporozoites The infective female Anopheles mosquito carries infectious stage of Plasmodium vivax called sporozoite in its salivary gland. When it bites a healthy person for sucking blood, large numbers of sporozoites are inoculated along with saliva. It pours saliva at the time of blood sucking because it contains anticoagulants which prevent the clotting of blood so that it is able to suck blood continuously. Structure of a sporozoite under electron microscopy is given below:

Figure 8.1.15 Structure of sporozoite i. Sporozoite is a microscopic, unnucleated, and sickle shaped structure with somewhat tapering ends. It measures about 12µ length and 1µ width. ii. It is externally covered by a thin, firm and elastic membrane called pellicle. iii. It shows wriggling movement because of the presence of longitudinally arranged contractile microtubules. iv. Paired organelles which secrete lytic juice, open into apical cap at the anterior end.

Lytic juice helps in the penetration of targeted cells of host. v. Similarly, convoluted tubules of unknown function, a centrally placed large prominent nucleus and a mitochondrion are also found embedded in the cytoplasm.
